passage: In Vienna, Vera had put up with Selin's taunts about her accent for six weeks: every corridor, every group photo. One evening she made a plan in her bedroom: an edited picture of Selin, a mocking caption, and a post on the class channel at midnight so everyone would see. "She deserves it," Vera told her friend Lena, who wrote back, "Are you sure?" Vera posted it anyway. By morning Selin had posted something crueler, and the class split into two camps. At break the head teacher called both girls to the office. The first question was about the post. The taunts, which Vera had never reported, were not mentioned at all, and both girls lost a week on the school channel.

qa.q: How long had Vera put up with Selin's taunts?
qa.a: Vera had put up with them for six weeks.

qa.q: What was Vera feeling when she made the plan in her bedroom?
qa.a: Vera felt angry and humiliated, and wanted Selin to feel the same way.

qa.q: What could Vera do instead, and why?
qa.a: Vera could show the taunts to a teacher or counsellor and keep a record, because that puts the original harm at the centre and does not risk punishment.

qa.q: How might Selin see Vera's post?
qa.a: Selin would probably see it as an attack and feel embarrassed and defensive, which fits with answering it with something crueler.

grounding: Angry at repeated taunts, the student plans to embarrass the bully online, which escalates, leads to punishment for both, and shifts attention from the original harm.

In the empty computer lab during lunch, Jomon showed Minakshi the clip on his phone: Rakesh tripping over his own bag in PT, edited with a clown sound.

"He's called me 'bin boy' every day for a month," Jomon said. "Tonight this goes on the class page."

Minakshi frowned. "Then it's you in trouble too. And everyone forgets what he did to you."

"I don't care."

He posted it that night. By morning it had been shared forty times, and Rakesh's friends had posted something worse about Jomon.

At ten, both boys were called to the vice-principal's office. For twenty minutes she asked only about the clip. When Jomon finally blurted out the month of name-calling, she stopped. "Why didn't I hear this first?" Before lunch she had called the counsellor and both families, and she gave both boys detention. Jomon walked out feeling he had turned himself into the problem.

qa.q: How many times had the clip been shared by morning?
qa.a: By morning it had been shared forty times.

qa.q: How did Jomon feel walking out of the vice-principal's office?
qa.a: Jomon felt regretful and frustrated, sensing he had turned himself into the problem instead of Rakesh's bullying.

qa.q: What approach could Jomon have taken instead of posting the clip?
qa.a: He could have written down the month of name-calling and shown it to a teacher or the counsellor, so the original harm stayed at the centre.

qa.q: How did the situation look to the vice-principal at first?
qa.a: At first she saw two boys trading online attacks, and only learned about the month of name-calling late, which is why she asked why she had not heard it first.

grounding: Shows a student retaliating by embarrassing a bully online, which escalates, brings punishment to both and shifts attention from the original harm.

passage:
Dear Ritu,

I did something stupid, and I need to tell someone who won't lecture me.

You know Sanya has been mocking my weight in front of the whole class since June. Last week I got a photo of her mid-sneeze at the science fair, face all scrunched. I made it into a sticker and put it on our class chat with a nasty caption.

For one night it felt amazing. Then her friends made worse stickers of me. Then someone forwarded the whole thing to our class teacher.

On Monday Sanya and I both sat outside the principal's office. Everyone talked about my sticker. Nobody talked about five months of her comments.

That evening Mamma sat with me, read everything, and said none of Sanya's cruelty was okay, and neither was mine. She called my class teacher right then to ask for a meeting about both.

Damini

qa.q: How long had Sanya been mocking Damini?
qa.a: Since June; Damini writes about five months of her comments.

qa.q: How did Damini feel after the first night?
qa.a: Damini felt ashamed and trapped, since the brief thrill turned into worse stickers and blame.

qa.q: What could Damini have done instead of making the sticker?
qa.a: Damini could have kept a record of Sanya's comments and taken it to Mamma or a teacher, so the adults saw the months of mockery first.

qa.q: How might the class teacher see the situation after Mamma's call?
qa.a: The teacher would likely see two problems to address, the months of mockery and the sticker, and could set up the meeting to deal with both fairly.

grounding: A letter shows a student retaliating online against a bully, escalating the conflict, bringing punishment to both and drawing attention from the original harm.
